policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'And he came also to Derbe' renders the adverbial kai; the omission would leave 'also' unaccounted for.
English repeats 'to' before a second place-name as a matter of idiom, so 'to Derbe and to Lystra' does not show whether the second eis stood in the Greek.
The same verse renders tis as 'a certain disciple', but the mother is simply 'a Jewess that believed' with no 'certain', so the added tinos is absent.
'they all knew that his father was a Greek' is the ordinary English for either the hoti-clause alone or the proleptic accusative, which ASV would smooth the same way.
Two imperfect spellings of the same verb; 'they delivered them the decrees' renders either.
A repeated article before 'elders' has no English exponent in 'the apostles and elders'.
Both forms of the place-name are rendered 'Jerusalem'.
ASV makes v.6 a complete sentence with the finite 'they went through the region ... having been forbidden'; the participial Dielthontes would leave the clause hanging until the verb of v.7.
The text reads 'the region of Phrygia and Galatia', one region qualified by both adjectives under a single article; a second article would give two members, which ASV records only in the margin.
ASV opens a verse with 'and' as a matter of course, so the connective does not distinguish de from its absence.
'to go into Bithynia' renders eis; kata would give 'toward' or 'along', not entry.
Aorist and present infinitive alike are rendered 'to go'.
ASV reads 'the Spirit of Jesus', naming Iesou.
'in the night' supplies the English article regardless of whether tes stood before nyktos.
Word order only; 'a vision appeared to Paul in the night' follows English order either way.
Word order only; 'There was a man of Macedonia' renders both arrangements.
ASV punctuates the participles as a series, 'standing, beseeching him, and saying'; English commas in such a chain neither require nor exclude the first kai.
An article before the place-name has no exponent in 'into Macedonia'.
ASV reads 'concluding that God had called us', theos rather than kyrios.
'Setting sail therefore from Troas' renders the inferential oun, not de.
'from Troas' shows no article either way.
de and te are both carried by the connective 'and the day following'.
Both the two-word and the compound form are transliterated 'Neapolis'.
Both readings mean 'and from thence', which is what ASV prints.
'the first of the district' takes prote as nominative with the genitive meridos, which excludes the NA reading 'of the first district'; the further article before Macedonia is invisible in English.
'we were in this city' renders the demonstrative taute, not aute.
'we went forth without the gate' renders pyles; poleos would give 'out of the city'.

The text reads 'where we supposed there was a place of prayer', the first person plural with the accusative; ASV puts the impersonal 'where was wont to be' in the margin as a variant of other authorities.
An article with theos has no exponent in 'one that worshipped God'.
Present and aorist imperative alike are rendered 'abide there'.
'to the place of prayer' supplies the English article whether or not ten stood in the Greek.
The margin glosses the Greek as 'a spirit, a Python', an appositional accusative; the genitive Pythonos would be glossed 'a spirit of Python'.
Both compounds mean 'met us'.
ASV renders a contemporaneous aorist participle with '-ing' as readily as a present, so 'following after Paul and us' does not settle the aspect.
'who proclaim unto you the way of salvation' renders the second person hymin.
An article with a proper name has no exponent in 'But Paul'.
'in the name of Jesus Christ' supplies the English article either way.
te and de are both carried by the connective 'And when they had laid'.
Aorist and perfect participle alike are rendered 'having received such a charge'.
Word order only; 'made their feet fast' renders both arrangements.
de and te are both carried by the connective 'and suddenly there was'.
The article has no exponent in the English of this clause.
The four readings differ only in word order and in the article with Paulos; 'But Paul cried with a loud voice' renders any of them.
The article is invisible in 'fell down before Paul and Silas'.
ASV reads 'Believe on the Lord Jesus' with no 'Christ'.
The text reads 'the word of the Lord' and the margin assigns 'God' to some ancient authorities.
'unto him, with all that were in his house' renders syn; kai would coordinate the hearers, 'to him and to all'.
Both forms are rendered 'all his'.
ASV renders an article with a household noun as a possessive, so 'into his house' does not require autou.
Two spellings of the same aorist, both 'rejoiced greatly'.
ASV reads 'reported the words to Paul' with no demonstrative, where v.38 renders tous logous toutous as 'these words'.
English requires an object with 'beaten' and 'cast', so the pronouns in 'They have beaten us ... and have cast us into prison' would stand whether or not this hemas was in the Greek.
Both compounds are rendered 'reported'.
'and they feared when they heard' carries either the postpositive de or the prefixed kai.
'they asked them to go away from the city' renders apelthein apo; exelthein with the genitive would be 'to go out of the city'.
'they went out of the prison' is the idiomatic English for exelthontes with either apo or ek.

ASV makes 'the brethren' the object of seeing and a pronoun the object of comforting, 'when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them', which is the RP order with autous; the base puts tous adelphous with parekalesan.
